page: Hetzner Cloud cx33 is an entry-tier virtual server from the Cost Optimized family, operating under the QEMU hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 4 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, complemented by 16 MB of L3 cache and 4 MB of L2 cache. The host configuration pairs these 4 vCPUs with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per vCPU, along with 80 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Hardware accelerators are not present.

Benchmark outcomes position the cx33 primarily within median and lower-quartile performance bands. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves 2672.38 in single-core and 10641.52 in multi-core throughput, both matching mid-tier averages. Standard Geekbench tests yield a single-core score of 1328.0, whereas the multi-core result of 4356.0 and code compilation scores place it in the lower 25 percent bracket. Memory bandwidth sustains 67.66 GB/sec for uncached read blocks and 49.67 GB/sec for write blocks, though PassMark memory performance ranks in the lower tier. In-memory caching via Redis demonstrates steady average results, executing 7.84 million SET operations per second.

Because the cx33 relies on shared vCPUs, users trade consistent sustained execution speeds for economical compute density. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation makes it efficient for non-critical services that do not require dedicated core isolation. Best-fit deployments include lightweight web services, dev/test environments, microservices, background job queues, and low-scale database or cache instances.
description: Hetzner Cloud cx33 is a budget-focused cloud instance featuring 4 shared AMD EPYC vCPUs clocked at 2.0 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. Configured with 8.0 GB of RAM and 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, the instance maintains a 1:2 memory-to-core profile without dedicated GPU acceleration. Benchmark assessments place its compute performance in the midrange for single-threaded stress tests and Redis operations (7.84 million SET ops/sec), while multi-core compilation and static web delivery register in the lower quartile due to the shared-core scheduling. With its cost-conscious design and integrated high-speed local storage, the cx33 serves as an efficient platform for staging environments, development tasks, microservice routing, and low-demand application hosting.
